2) 6-month reserved (short tenor) with a larger up-front credit (5%) and a one-time right to pause add-on capacity at 30 days' notice.

Sofia — quick read from finance perspective: 6-month tenor with 5% up-front credit is borderline but workable provided we introduce two mitigations:

1) Price Adjustment Band: Accept the 12% upward trigger but cap Redwood exposure to a 50% pass-through of index movements beyond the trigger (i.e., we absorb first half of delta up to contract cap).
2) Minimum monthly commitment floor: ensure Cognify retains a minimum monthly usage level (20% of reserved) or we reserve the right to claw back credits pro-rata.

Operationally, the 48h burst SLA is tough for all customers but may be acceptable for EU region if we define "burst" quantitatively and allow a staged response (48h for allocation + 72h for extra GPUs if procurement involves third-party cloud spot buys). Legal will need to draft the exact SLA language.

If legal is comfortable with those mitigations, I can sign off and we can present back to Cognify with a revised SOW and DocuSign link.

— Marcus

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity term and GPU price-sensitivity — final proposal

Emma — thank you for the clear feedback. We can accept the short-tenor structure with the following negotiated terms: 

- 6-month reserved commitment with 5% up-front credit to Cognify.
- Price-sensitivity trigger set at 12% upward movement vs. agreed vendor benchmark. If trigger fires, Redwood will:
    • open a one-time renegotiation; OR
    • apply a credit equal to 50% of the excess cost delta to Cognify's invoices (Redwood absorbs first 50% of delta beyond the trigger, subject to a cap equal to 10% of total reserved spend).
- Minimum monthly usage floor of 20% of reserved capacity; credits subject to pro-rata adjustment if floor not met.
- Burst SLA: Redwood commits to allocation acknowledgement within 48 hours and best-effort provisioning within 72 hours for additional GPUs; production-critical expedited provisioning (under 24h) is an add-on.

I've attached an updated SOW and pricing workbook reflecting these terms. If this is acceptable, I will send the DocuSign and legal redlines for signature (we normally require a board-level approver for any cap exceptions).

Next steps: please confirm by end of day Friday and we'll issue the DocuSign envelope.

Best — Sofia
